title: Quantum sensing of low-frequency electric signal enabled by modulated auxiliary field in Rydberg atoms
authors: Xiayang Fan, Shenchao Jin, Jiatian Liu, Jialiang Zhang, Qichao Qi, Yuan Sun
abstract: Rydberg atoms have emerged as a versatile and efficient platform for high-sensitivity quantum sensing of free-space electric fields, with remarkable progress in detecting low-frequency signals. To date, low-frequency Rydberg receivers have relied on a constant bias field, typically realized via intra-cell electrodes or Rydberg plasmas generated by photoelectric effects or inter-atomic interactions. While these approaches improve sensitivity, they suffer from inherent challenges in calibration, long-term stability, and robustness, hindering practical deployment. Here, we propose, design, and experimentally demonstrate a quantum sensing scheme for low-frequency electric signals using modulated auxiliary fields in Rydberg atoms. Unlike conventional methods that employ external DC electric fields that are often fully shielded by adsorbed atom layers on the cell walls, we introduce an AC-field modulation strategy. The incoming low-frequency signal mixes with the auxiliary field, and together they induce Stark shifts of the Rydberg level. These shifts are mapped onto the probe laser via electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT), in a manner analogous to heterodyne detection. We demonstrate a sensitivity of $7.5 \pm 2.6~\mathrm{μV/(cm\cdot Hz^{1/2})}$ at 5 kHz and a minimal detectable field of $0.26 \pm 0.04~\mathrm{μV/cm}$ with an integration time of 1000 s. Furthermore, we extend this approach to systematically analyze the performance of generalized auxiliary fields containing multiple frequency components. By virtue of modulated auxiliary field and quantum frequency mixing, our results establish a robust and systematic framework for quantum sensing of low-frequency electric fields with Rydberg atoms, offering improved sensitivity, stability, and immunity to environmental drifts.
summary: The paper introduces an advanced quantum sensing technique for measuring weak, low-frequency electric fields using Rydberg atoms. By employing a modulated auxiliary AC field and leveraging Quantum Frequency Mixing (QFM), the method generates a measurable cross-term Stark shift read out via EIT. This approach significantly improves stability and sensitivity compared to older methods, establishing a robust platform for next-generation quantum sensors.
main_problem: To develop a quantum sensing scheme for low-frequency (LF) electric signals that overcomes the inherent instability and calibration issues of conventional DC bias field methods.
main_result: The authors demonstrated high sensitivity ($7.5 \pm 2.6 \, \mu	ext{V}/(	ext{cm} \cdot 	ext{Hz}^{1/2})$ at $5 \, 	ext{kHz}$) and achieved a minimal detectable field of $0.26 \pm 0.04 \, \mu	ext{V}/	ext{cm}$ after long integration times.
method: The scheme uses Quantum Frequency Mixing (QFM) by modulating an auxiliary AC field ($	ext{E}_{	ext{aux}}$), allowing the incoming LF signal ($	ext{E}_{	ext{sig}}$) to mix with it. This shift is then read out via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency (EIT).
model_or_system: The physical platform is Rydberg atoms in an atomic vapor cell, utilizing a second-order Stark shift induced by the total electric field ($	ext{E}_{	ext{tot}}$). The detection relies on mapping the resulting energy shift onto the probe laser intensity via EIT.
key_observables: Transmitted light intensity $I(t)$, which is related to the cross-term Stark shift $\delta_{	ext{cr}}$, and the reconstructed signal amplitude $|Z|$.
important_parameters: Sensitivity of $7.5 \pm 2.6 \, \mu	ext{V}/(	ext{cm} \cdot 	ext{Hz}^{1/2})$ at $5 \, 	ext{kHz}$; minimal detectable field $\propto T^{-0.48}$ with integration time $T$.
main_assumptions: The method assumes the cross-term ($\delta_{	ext{cr}}$) dominates and is linearly proportional to the signal field, allowing for robust reconstruction.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the experimental setup, the principle of modulated auxiliary fields and QFM, and the signal reconstruction process. Figure 2 details the verification of the cross-term using combined fields and the subsequent signal reconstruction method.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem with conventional methods, proposes the AC modulation/QFM scheme, details the theoretical modeling (cross-term generation), presents experimental validation for LF signals, extends the concept to multi-frequency analysis via Maximal Ratio Combining (MRC), and concludes by establishing a robust framework.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it adapts established quantum optics techniques (QFM) from RF/MW regimes into the challenging low-frequency electric field domain using Rydberg atoms, providing a stable alternative to traditional DC biasing methods.
